issues.title: [Bug]: empty list/record types (`int[0]`, `never[]`, `record {||}`) are treated as subtypes of `readonly`, so mutable empty values become immutable
issues.output:
true
true
error: inherent type violation: cannot mutate readonly value
        at clearAll(1768.bal:4)
           main(1768.bal:14)

Also: `int[0] z = []; readonly r = z;` compiles, while `z.removeAll()` fails with error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: cannot update 'readonly' value of type '[never...]'
issues.edge_case_reason: Empty list types such as int[0] / never[] and record {||} are rarely used
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. The program prints true/true and then panics, instead of false/false/0. The front end treats the empty list type as a subtype of readonly: `readonly r = z` is accepted (a missing diagnostic) and `z.removeAll()` is wrongly rejected. The emitted `newArray [never...]` then gets the readonly bit at runtime through the same semtype subtyping check. A clean-context spec check found the issue VALID: per §6.7.1 the readonly bit is set only when the expected type is a subtype of readonly, and per §5.7.5 int[0] also contains the mutable empty-list shape. The root cause is in semtypes/type checking (wrong compile-time diagnostics), so this is frontend; bir_ok is false because the compiler wrongly accepts/rejects code. Related but not a duplicate: #1424, #1044, #1753.

issues.title: [Bug]: record type including records with different rest descriptors (implicit `anydata...` vs `string...`) is not rejected
issues.edge_case_reason: Combines two record inclusions with conflicting rest descriptors, one of them implicit; this is rare
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: the program compiles and prints {"a":1,"b":2}. A clean-context spec check found the issue VALID: §5.4.2.2 makes it an error when two inclusions bring different record-rest-descriptors that the including type does not override, and an inclusive record counts as `anydata...`. This is a missing diagnostic, so frontend. Related but not a duplicate: #1452 (the implicit anydata... rest is dropped on inclusion), probably the same code area.

issues.title: [Bug]: `x !is T` narrows a mutable list variable by plain set difference instead of `-ro`, rejecting valid `==`/`push`
issues.edge_case_reason: Needs !is narrowing of a mutable union-element list against another list type, which depends on the subtle -ro rule
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: a valid program is rejected. A clean-context spec check found the issue VALID: narrowing in the false branch uses Tx −ro T, and for mutable lists (int|string)[] −ro int[] = (int|string)[]. The intersection with int[] is non-empty, so == is allowed (§6.29), and at runtime the result is `eq`. Frontend (type narrowing). Related: #1593 is the same −ro rule with a different symptom (removing a mutable member from a union). It is not a duplicate, but the two may share a fix.

issues.title: [Bug]: non-reserved query clause keywords (`conflict`, `outer`, `limit`, `order`, `where`, `select`, `by`, `join`) can't be used as identifiers
issues.output:
error[SYNTAX_ERROR]: missing function name
 --> 1771.bal:3:10
error[SYNTAX_ERROR]: invalid token
 --> 1771.bal:3:18
issues.edge_case_reason: Ordinary code: identifiers like `limit`, `order` and `select` are common names
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: a SYNTAX_ERROR on a valid program. A clean-context spec check found the issue VALID: the 2024R1 grammar marks conflict/outer/join/limit/order/by/where/select (and group/collect) as NR (not reserved), while `equals` stays reserved. Parser/lexer issue, so frontend. Related but not a duplicate: #1620 (method names map/join/start).

issues.title: [Bug]: http:Client init takes ClientConfiguration positionally, so named config arguments fail to compile
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. This is standard library (ballerina/http) API behaviour: Nutcracker's http.bal declares `init(string url, ClientConfiguration config = {})`, while the Ballerina http module's public API uses an included record parameter `*ClientConfiguration`, so named configuration arguments must be accepted. Valid as a library API-compatibility bug. Category: library.

issues.title: [Bug]: http listener answers 404 instead of 400 when a typed path parameter fails to convert
issues.output: GET /api/items/abc -> HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found {"status":404,...,"message":"no matching resource found for path"}; GET /api/items/5 -> item
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main (I ran the listener and sent requests with curl). This is http library behaviour, not language semantics: the path matches the resource but the typed path parameter fails to bind, which the http module answers with 400 Bad Request. Returning 404 misreports a client data error as a missing route. Valid library bug. Category: library.

issues.title: [Bug]: http `getHeaders` result fails `is string[]`
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: prints false. Per the spec, a function's return value must belong to its declared return type (string[]|HeaderNotFoundError). The type test checks the inherent type of the mutable list, so the native code must create the list with inherent type string[]; the issue points at newListValue in http_native.go. Valid; the bug is in the http native library code. Category: library.

issues.title: [Bug]: http `Response.addHeader("Content-Type", ...)` keeps every value
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Content-Type is single-valued (RFC 9110 §8.3), and the Ballerina http module replaces it on addHeader. Valid http library behaviour bug. Category: library.
